questions.question: Intersection over Union (IoU) between two bounding boxes is computed as:

options.text: Area of intersection divided by area of union
Area of union divided by area of intersection
Sum of areas minus intersection
Intersection area divided by image area

questions.explanation: IoU = |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|, ranging from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (perfect).

questions.question: What problem do anchor boxes help solve in object detectors?

options.text: They remove the need for a classification head
They provide reference shapes for predicting objects of varying sizes and aspect ratios
They replace non-max suppression
They eliminate the need for training data

questions.explanation: Anchors provide a set of prior box shapes at each spatial location, so the network predicts offsets relative to them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of non-maximum suppression (NMS) in detection?

options.text: To increase recall by keeping all predictions
To remove redundant overlapping boxes, keeping the highest-scoring one
To normalize bounding box coordinates
To compute the loss function

questions.explanation: NMS removes duplicate detections of the same object by suppressing lower-scoring boxes that overlap a higher-scoring one above an IoU threshold.

questions.question: Focal Loss modifies cross-entropy to address what problem?

options.text: Vanishing gradients
The extreme foreground/background class imbalance in dense detectors
Overfitting small models
Learning rate decay

questions.explanation: Focal loss down-weights easy examples so that training focuses on hard, misclassified examples — critical for one-stage detectors like RetinaNet.

questions.question: What does a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) provide?

options.text: A smaller model for embedded devices
Multi-scale feature maps enabling detection of objects at various sizes
Quantized inference
A replacement for the backbone network

questions.explanation: FPN builds a top-down pathway with lateral connections, producing feature maps at multiple scales with rich semantics at each.
